title: Smoky Red Pepper Aioli
description: Peeled sweet pepper and smoked paprika give this garlicky dipping sauce a deep red color and gentle heat.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: plain full-fat mayonnaise
ingredients.note: Use plain commercial mayonnaise made with pasteurized eggs.

steps.title: Concentrate the pepper
steps.text: Simmer {pepper}, {garlic}, {paprika} and {vinegar} in the HexClad for 4–6 minutes, stirring, until most of the loose liquid has evaporated.

steps.title: Cool the puree
steps.text: Blend the pepper mixture smooth. Press it through the sieve into a bowl and refrigerate for about 10 minutes until cold.

steps.title: Whisk the aioli
steps.text: Fold the cold red pepper puree into {mayo} until the color is uniform.

steps.title: Adjust the consistency
steps.text: Scrape all of the mixture into the measuring cup. Add cold water a teaspoon at a time if needed to reach about 1 cup, maintaining a smooth spoonable texture.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chill covered for 15 minutes and spoon alongside saucy chicken cutlets or tender potato wedges.

notes: Yield: About 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Cook the pepper puree a day ahead and fold it into the mayonnaise on serving day. Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The mayonnaise can separate and release liquid after thawing. Fridge reheat: Serve chilled. Stir until smooth just before portioning. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw covered in the refrigerator, then whisk or blend briefly and serve cold. Option A uses sherry vinegar and smoked paprika. For gentler Option B, omit the vinegar and use half as much sweet unsmoked paprika. The aioli is dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 132 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 0.8 g total carbohydrate, 14.2 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 121 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
